newsitem.title: USA: 1997 dollar outlook negative says Goldman research.
newsitem.headline: 1997 dollar outlook negative says Goldman research.

text.p: Goldman Sachs research said the dollar exchange rate will peak on technicals and interest rate differentials against the mark and yen in the first quarter of next year before falling well below current levels by the year-end 1997.

Currency market technical indicators and movements in national interest rates will help fuel a dollar rise in the first quarter of 1997, possibly peaking above Goldman's 1.58 mark and 115 yen forecast for the end of January, the bank said in a weekly research report dated December 17.

However, Goldman predicted the U.S. unit's exchange rate will drop to 1.45 marks and 105 yen by the end of 1997 due to an accelerated economic recovery in Germany and Japan increasing the risk associated with the U.S. balance of payments deficit.
"Left unchecked, we expect that chronically large U.S. current account deficits are likely to have a negative impact on the long-term value of the U.S. dollar," the report said.
Goldman's three- and six-month 1997 forecasts were for 1.55 and 1.50 marks, and 110 and 106 yen, respectively.
The firm also projected heightened rate volatility next year, due to "bigger uncertainties". A dollar trading range of 1.40 to 1.65 marks and 100 to 125 yen was expected.
In early trade on Wednesday, the dollar traded at 1.5530/38 marks and 113.58/68 yen.
